1. A device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:a microneedle;
an electrode material on the microneedle;
a biorecognition layer on the electrode material, the biorecognition layer comprising a polymer, a biorecognition element configured to react with the analyte, and an interferent blocking agent that fills voids within the polymer, at least a portion of the interferent blocking agent being in contact with the electrode material; and
a diffusion-limiting layer on the biorecognition layer.
2. The device of claim 1, wherein the interferent blocking agent is a non-conducting polymer.
3. The device of claim 1, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises one or more of resorcinol, hydroquinone quinol, 2-amino-4,6-dinitro phenol picramic acid, 3,5-dihydroxy toluene orcinol, 2,4,6-trinitro resorcinol styphnic acid, 2-hydroxy phenol catechol, 9-phenanthrol, pyrogallol, a-napthhol, anisole, phenetole, picric acid, and phenol.
4. The device of claim 3, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises phenol.
5. The device of claim 4, wherein the phenol is present within the biorecognition layer at a concentration of between about 0.1 mg/ml or 0.01% w/v and about 10 mg/ml or 1% w/v.
6. The device of claim 4, wherein polymerized phenol is entrapped within the voids of the polymer.
7. The device of claim 1, wherein interference current at the electrode material of the device changes less than 70% over a one-week period.
8. The device of claim 1, wherein the biorecognition element is physically entrapped within the polymer.
9. The device of claim 1, wherein the polymer comprises one or more of aniline, acetylene,
phenylene, phenylene vinylene, phenylene diamine, thiophene, 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene, and aminophenylboronic acid.
10. A device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:a microneedle;
an electrode material on the microneedle;
a biorecognition layer on the electrode material, the biorecognition layer comprising a polymer, a biorecognition element configured to react with the analyte, and an interferent blocking agent that fills voids within the polymer, the voids traversing a thickness of the polymer; and
a diffusion-limiting layer on the biorecognition layer.
11. The device of claim 10, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises one or more of resorcinol, hydroquinone quinol, 2-amino-4,6-dinitro phenol picramic acid, 3,5-dihydroxy toluene orcinol, 2,4,6-trinitro resorcinol styphnic acid, 2-hydroxy phenol catechol, 9-phenanthrol, pyrogallol, a-napthhol, anisole, phenetole, picric acid, and phenol.
12. The device of claim 11, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises phenol.
13. The device of claim 12, wherein the phenol is present within the biorecognition layer at a concentration of between about 0.1 mg/ml or 0.01% w/v and about 10 mg/ml or 1% w/v.
14. The device of claim 12, wherein polymerized phenol is entrapped within the voids of the polymer.
15. The device of claim 10, wherein interference current at the electrode material of the device changes less than 10% over a one-week period.
16. The device of claim 10, wherein at least a portion of the voids are exposed to a surface of the electrode material.
17. The device of claim 10, wherein the interferent blocking agent fills at least about 80% of the voids within the polymer to limit access by interferents to the electrode material.
18. The device of claim 10, wherein the polymer comprises one or more of aniline, acetylene, phenylene, phenylene vinylene, phenylene diamine, thiophene, 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene, and aminophenylboronic acid.
19. The device of claim 10, wherein the diffusion-limiting layer comprises one or more of polydimethylsiloxane, polyurethane, polyvinyl chloride, polyvinylpyrrolidone, polycarbonate, polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyester, high density polyethylene, low density polyethylene, and polytetrafluoroethylene.
20. A device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:a microneedle;
a working electrode on the microneedle, the working electrode comprising an electrode material on the microneedle; and
a biorecognition layer on the electrode material, the biorecognition layer comprising a polymer, a biorecognition element configured to react with the analyte, and an interferent blocking agent that fills voids within the polymer.
21. The device of claim 20, wherein the interferent blocking agent limits access by interferents to the electrode material.
22. The device of claim 20, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises one or more of resorcinol, hydroquinone quinol, 2-amino-4,6-dinitro phenol picramic acid, 3,5-dihydroxy toluene orcinol, 2,4,6-trinitro resorcinol styphnic acid, 2-hydroxy phenol catechol, 9-phenanthrol, pyrogallol, a-napthhol, anisole, phenetole, picric acid, and phenol.
23. The device of claim 22, wherein the interferent blocking agent comprises phenol.
24. The device of claim 23, wherein polymerized phenol is entrapped within the voids of the polymer.
25. The device of claim 20, wherein interference current at the electrode material of the device changes less than 70% over a one-week period.
26. The device of claim 20, wherein the device further comprises a microneedle array comprising a first plurality of microneedles each comprising a working electrode, the first plurality of microneedles including the microneedle, the microneedle array further comprising a second microneedle comprising a reference electrode and a third microneedle comprising a counter electrode,wherein the microneedle array further comprises a second plurality of microneedles each comprising a counter electrode, the second plurality of microneedles including the third microneedle, and
wherein the first plurality of microneedles is arranged between the second microneedle and the second plurality of microneedles.
27. The device of claim 20, wherein the device further comprises a microneedle array comprising a first plurality of microneedles each comprising a working electrode, the first plurality of microneedles including the microneedle, the microneedle array further comprising a second microneedle comprising a reference electrode and a third microneedle comprising a counter electrode, wherein each of the working electrodes is electrically connected to the counter electrode such that current flows from each of the working electrodes to the counter electrode.
28. The device of claim 20, wherein the device further comprises
a microneedle array comprising a first plurality of microneedles each comprising a working electrode, the first plurality of microneedles including the microneedle, the microneedle array further comprising a second microneedle comprising a reference electrode, a third microneedle comprising a counter electrode, anda second plurality of microneedles each comprising a counter electrode, the second plurality of microneedles including the third microneedle,
wherein each of the counter electrodes is electrically connected to the working electrodes, and wherein a majority of current from a first working electrode of the working electrodes flows to a first counter electrode of the counter electrodes, the first counter electrode positioned nearest the first working electrode relative to any other counter electrode.
29. The device of claim 28, wherein the working electrodes comprise three working electrodes and the counter electrodes comprise three counter electrodes, the three working electrodes forming a barrier separating the reference electrode from the three counter electrodes.
30. A method for manufacturing a device for use in sensing an analyte, comprising:depositing a biorecognition element and a polymer on an electrode material disposed on a microneedle, wherein the biorecognition element is configured to react with the analyte;
applying an interferent blocking agent to the polymer after deposition, thereby filling voids within the polymer with the interferent blocking agent; and
depositing a diffusion-limiting layer on the polymer.
